questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of these, except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also protects you if you crash.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Only take a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to perform.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: You should inspect your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, all of these are hazards, except:

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects being thrown from other vehicles.
Blasts of wind.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Also be aware of wind gusts from the passing vehicle and objects that passengers might throw without paying attention to the road.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.

options.text: Farther away, more slowly
Farther away, faster
Closer, more slowly
Closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it harder for other drivers to judge where you are and how fast you are going.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:

options.text: Downshifting.
Upshifting.
Cross-shifting.
Rolling on the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: You can slow down by downshifting. Remember that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights, so other drivers may not know you are slowing down.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Increase your speed.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that are slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Ride under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, cover the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if you need to.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can get a better view of the uneven surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact shock. This prevents the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another car), use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see, and wear reflective materials to be visible. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: When you stop your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Not worry about them and just focus on the road in front of you.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only increase danger. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers don't expect you there and may swerve onto the shoulder suddenly.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Always slow down.
Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
Accelerate hard.
Not worry about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly through the turn.

questions.question: When do you need less space cushion between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When you cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
When traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: You need a larger space cushion in bad conditions. Increase your following distance when pavement is slippery, you can't see through the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have a difficult time getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: You could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if danger occurs.

questions.question: When riding and turning, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Exit the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is especially dangerous when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to avoid the wet center. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They happen in the dark.
They involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your risk of crashing?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you change lanes.
Follow other drivers closely.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Don't use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others, signal your moves, keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: What should you do about mirror checks?

options.text: They are not important.
Check them only on long trips.
Check them as part of your regular scanning routine.
They don't help because you can't do anything about what's behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them as part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as you ride. Also check them before you change lanes, when you stop at an intersection, and before you slow down.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can reach the ground when you sit on it. You should be able to reach and use all the controls easily.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight shifts forward when braking, you:

options.text: Can brake harder with the front brake.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can brake harder with the rear brake.
Will lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can brake harder with the front brake.
questions.explanation: When your weight moves forward during braking, the front wheel has more grip on the road. This means you can apply the front brake with more pressure.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A parked car might pull out suddenly into your path.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for parking.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car might pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars present dangers. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors might open into your lane. Pedestrians might step out from between cars.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Make sudden movements.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When riding on slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, stopping:

options.text: Is easier than riding without a sidecar.
Takes longer than riding without a sidecar.
Is not possible.
Is about the same as riding without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes longer than riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which means you need more braking power to stop. Stopping always takes longer when going downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than you normally do.
Follow other vehicles more closely than when riding alone.
Ride faster than you normally do.
Start braking a little later than when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you normally do.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your distance from other vehicles, and use larger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders ride?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they feel most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This allows experienced riders at the back to watch them.
